feature: What the Measure tool does after a measurement lands
summary: You picked hand back to Select, so nothing on screen changed. What is new is proof: every one of the four Measure modes now provably hands the ruler back with the fresh measurement selected, and one press of I brings the tool back in the same mode you left it in, so a second measurement is one press plus one click.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png with File > Open. Flags are at their defaults.

try.do: Press I until the pill above the tool bar reads Size.
Click the Save Changes button. Two calipers land, the arrow comes back, and the width caliper is selected.
Click the Reset button. Nothing new lands: the arrow is in hand, so this is a plain click on the picture.
Press I once and click Reset again. It measures this time, in Size, without you re-picking the mode.
Press I twice for Gap, press Esc to put the tool down, then press I once. You come back in Gap, not in Distance.
Take a Distance: three clicks. On the third the number lands and the arrow comes back.
Press the left and right arrow keys. The measurement that just landed nudges, which is the reason the tool hands back at all.

evaluate: Measuring a second thing is now one press of I plus one click. Does that feel like the right cost, or still one press too many?

Changing mode after a landing costs the pickup press plus one press per mode. Sizing then gapping then aligning is where that adds up. Is walking the modes with I the right way to switch, or do you want each mode on its own key?
The mode pill rises again on every pickup, so it flashed once per measurement. Is that a useful reminder or noise by the fourth time?
A Size click lands two calipers but selects only the width one. Should the arrow keys nudge both?
Esc puts the tool down. Did you reach for Esc or for V?
rough: No code changed here beyond a comment. You chose today's behaviour, so this task's real output is the guard: Scripts/playtest/measure-handback.json walks Size, Gap, Distance and the pickup key on the real app and fails if the hand-back or the sticky mode ever regresses.
The pill re-raising on every pickup is the one cost of this choice that the walk still shows. It was listed as a con on the card and is left alone rather than quietly softened.
Alignment mode is not in the walk. It lands from a drag rather than a click, and its own walk already covers it.
The last Distance readout parked on top of the Copy to clipboard label. That is the readout-clearance question already open as its own task, not something this change caused.
